## 보관 원문

> # Wang et al. 2026 — low-temperature aqueous iron electrodeposition review
>
> - Title: Decarbonizing ironmaking through green-electricity-driven low-temperature electrodeposition: A comprehensive review of challenges in iron electroextraction from aqueous solutions
> - Journal: Hydrometallurgy, volume 244, article 106804
> - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.hydromet.2026.106804
> - Publisher page: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304386X26001763
> - Authors: Zhen Wang; Mengmeng Liu; Renze Xu
> - Collected: 2026-07-28
> - Peer review: journal review article
>
> ## Route comparison
>
> - The review separates low-temperature aqueous ironmaking into alkaline and
>   acidic electrolyte families rather than treating all aqueous electrolysis as
>   one route.
> - Alkaline systems can provide relatively high current efficiency and lower
>   corrosivity, but low iron-oxide solubility and slow solid-state mass transfer
>   constrain scale-up.
> - Acidic systems can accelerate electroreduction by reducing dissolved iron
>   ions, but hydrogen evolution and corrosion compete with iron deposition.
> - Both families operate near 100°C, far below conventional pyrometallurgical
>   temperatures, and can in principle be coupled directly to renewable
>   electricity.
>
> ## Industrialization boundary
>
> - The authors identify current efficiency, dense and manageable product form,
>   real-ore impurity handling, electrode design, reactor configuration and
>   variable-renewable integration as unresolved engineering challenges.
> - The paper is a cross-route academic synthesis, not evidence that a named
>   company's demonstration plant has achieved design throughput, continuous
>   operation, commercial cost or product qualification.
> - Electra's acidic electrowinning and alkaline slurry routes such as SIDERWIN
>   therefore require separate project-level evidence even when they share the
>   label “low-temperature aqueous electrolysis.”
